message.text: I need to identify the persistent entity types defined in the store package, like Memo, User, Attachment, Reaction, and similar structs, then check how often they're referenced outside the store package by searching for their usage.
I'm cataloging the main entity types like Attachment, Memo, and User, then checking how many packages outside the store layer reference each type to gauge their usage spread across the codebase.

args.command:
cd /bench/repo
for t in Memo User Attachment Reaction MemoShare MemoRelation UserSetting UserIdentity Inbox InstanceSetting IdentityProvider; do
  files=$(grep -rlE "store\.$t\b" --include="*.go" server internal cmd 2>/dev/null | grep -v "_test.go")
  pkgs=$(echo "$files" | xargs -n1 dirname 2>/dev/null | sort -u | wc -l)
  fcount=$(echo "$files" | grep -c . )
  echo "$t: files=$fcount pkgs=$pkgs"
done

message.text: I'm checking whether UserSetting is used via the protobuf type or the store struct directly, since server methods likely take store.UserSetting or a pointer to it. I want to make sure my regex pattern correctly matches both the value and pointer forms.

I realize my grep approach undercounts because Go relies heavily on type inference — code often uses `store.UserSetting` only implicitly through variables and method returns, without spelling out the type literally in the source.

I need a more reliable method: search broadly for actual `store.X` type usages in function signatures and imports across the whole repo excluding the store directory itself, rather than just specific folders, since some undercounts could stem from checking too narrow a scope.

args.command:
cd /bench/repo
for t in Memo User Attachment Reaction MemoShare MemoRelation UserSetting UserIdentity Inbox InstanceSetting IdentityProvider; do
  files=$(grep -rlE "store\.$t\b" --include="*.go" . 2>/dev/null | grep -v "_test.go" | grep -v "^./store/")
  pkgs=$(echo "$files" | xargs -n1 dirname 2>/dev/null | sort -u)
  pkgcount=$(echo "$pkgs" | grep -c .)
  fcount=$(echo "$files" | grep -c . )
  echo "$t: files=$fcount pkgs=$pkgcount"
done
